executive_assessment.text: Local depth includes Restauración/Dajabón farming and adaptation barriers, cited informal housing in Greater Santo Domingo and Puerto Plata, and wealth- and gender-differentiated flood vulnerability.
A modeled border-service and resource-allocation mechanism can inform inclusive planning, but does not establish climate-driven violence or migrant threat propensity.

National evidence describes water-service inequities, social-protection targeting and intergovernmental coordination constraints, with historical disaster impacts kept separate from forecasts and current delivery.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2024 reports: Interviewees in Restauración, Dajabón, linked rainfall shifts and land degradation to lower farm yields and migration intentions.
Source dated 2024 reports: Some Restauración farmers diversified into forestry and agroforestry; local association nurseries provided plants, but time, land and investment constrained poorer farmers.
Source dated 2023-04 reports: The note cites estimates that informal settlements house 43% of Greater Santo Domingo residents and 70% of Puerto Plata residents.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 13 of 13 evidence records and 1 of 1 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
DOM is absent from EXISTING_COUNTRIES.json and no countries/DOM baseline dossier was present; this is a new-country extraction, not an extension of an existing record.

The strongest direct climate–FCV evidence is a modeled, conditional climate-migration pathway with potential host–migrant tension; the reviewed primary sources do not establish observed climate-driven violence in the Dominican Republic.
No reviewed primary source linked insecurity or conflict to interrupted Dominican climate adaptation or disaster response. Not found is not evidence of absence.

The Ministry of Environment adaptation-plan link returned HTTP 500; the IMF Climate Policy Diagnostic formats returned internal errors; the 2025 health adaptation plan was discoverable only through metadata/abstract. Their text is not used.
The World Bank poverty note relies on a 2021 flood-risk survey for 2019–2021 impacts; climate-migration results are scenario-dependent model estimates, not observed forecasts.

The modeled host–migrant tension mechanism is conditional on infrastructure and policy, not a statement that migrants are a security threat. Mobility can be adaptive and no observed violence is attributed.
The 2021 survey is not representative at regional/provincial scale; local housing shares are cited secondary figures. Source-era data must not be presented as a 2026 local vulnerability ranking.
No reverse conflict-to-climate mechanism was established. Climate projections and response systems are not evaluated protection or integration outcomes.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
